answer: One defense is stake-backed reputation tied to a single cipher identity: each agent must lock a deposit under one public key before it can trade, and its reputation accrues only along that thread of past transactions. New identities start with zero trust, so an attacker who spawns many fake agents must fund every one of them and let each wander through real, costly work before earning any influence. Creating a thousand sock puppets then costs a thousand deposits plus time, while honest agents keep the reputation they already earned.
